observations: body L1-L2: the head is set in capitals and small capitals; the dash after «a)» measures 9.5 pt. The place is p. 147 of the translation, appendix D, on the stations of the planets.

body L3-L26: heavy brackets open and close Schiaparelli's addition, from «Totum» (L3) to «Schiaparelli.» (L26); a speck stands in the left margin before L3. «Albatenii» (L3), «al–Battānī» (L7), «Ptolemaeus» (L16) and «Interpolator» (L20) are letter-spaced; «Ptolemaeus» (L13) and «Interpolator» (L4, L15) are not. «354–55» has a long dash (5.3 pt), as have «al–Battānī» (5.4 pt) and «138–39» (L7, joined to the figures); the dashes after «praetereunt.» and «tribuere!» measure 9.8 and 10.2 pt. The hyphens of «Alma-», «con-» and «inter-» measure 2.5, 2.4 and 2.6 pt; that of «distan-» prints as a raised dot. The degree sign after «112» (L17) prints joined to the 2. The numbers of Saturn are those of the table of stations, vol. II, p. 138: 112° 45′ and 247° 15′ at 6° from the apogee of the eccentric, 115° 29′ and 244° 31′ at 180°, the two stations of each row adding up to 360°. The days of appendix D follow from them as L18-L19 describe: at the mean motion of the anomaly of Saturn, 360° in its synodic period of about 378.1 days or about 0° 57′ 8″ a day, 112° 45′ take 118.4 days (118 ½ on p. 147); the station of Mars from 157° 33′ to 169° 14′ of anomaly (p. 147, L22-L23), at about 0° 27′ 42″ a day, takes 25.3 days, the 25 ⅓ of L25 and of p. 147, L20 (the codex has 24 ⅓).

body L27-L31: «al–Kātib» has a long dash (5.2 pt). Note d on chapter L, p. 291, says that this name of Mercury, «scriba» or «scriptor», occurs only in appendix D (vol. III, p. 221, l. 15 of the text). «138–39» (L30) has a long dash (5.2 pt).

body L32-L35: the head is set in capitals and small capitals; the dash after «a)» measures 9.7 pt. Appendix E begins on p. 148 of the translation. «187–88» and «9–11» have long dashes (5.3 pt each). The promise is p. 129, L9-L11 of the translation («quarum usum in ultimo capitum post finem libri explicavimus»), as printed.
